A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeRP3D study. All 22 pages, including Appendices A–C, equations, Tables 1–10 and Figures 1–8, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original NeRP3D experiments on reconstruction, detection, occupancy prediction, map construction and generalization, including quantitative and qualitative appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their results in the main text and appendices, including Tables 1–10.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same point sampling, coordinate contraction, deformable attention, NeuS rendering, downstream adaptation and pre-training losses. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use nuScenes, Occ3D-nuScenes and Argoverse 2 with the same reconstruction, detection, occupancy, mapping and transfer scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including UniPAD and SelfOcc, GaussianPretrain in Table 4, VisionPAD in Table 5, and EmerNeRF and DistillNeRF variants in Tables 7–8.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes rendered RGB and depth image size from 1:2 to 1:4 of input size. Table 7 changes depth evaluation resolution for SelfOcc, UniPAD and NeRP3D from 400 × 225 to 200 × 112, retaining 114 × 64 for EmerNeRF/DistillNeRF. These are explicit reported-setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish that evaluations were rerun.

E4.justification: The transfer experiments, Section 4.5 ablation summaries, multi-resolution reconstruction analysis in Table 9, and cross-task retention analysis in Table 10 and Figure 8 are unchanged. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical result entries, rankings and qualitative examples are retained. For example, NeRP3D remains at 47.3 NDS and 42.8 mAP in Table 1 and 33.42 PSNR in Table 2. Revised resolution statements do not establish a performance change.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain identical coordinate, attention, rendering and loss formulations. No mathematical definition, derivation, assumption or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about continuous point representations, preserving pre-trained NeRF knowledge, avoiding conflicting view-transformation priors, and improving reconstruction and downstream perception.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning discretization, generalization and structural retention are unchanged. Both conclusions retain the limitations involving depth beyond the region of interest, reliance on LiDAR and computational costs.

D1.justification: The documented rendering/downsampling settings change in Section 4.2 and Table 7. Hardware, optimizer, epochs, loss weights, input resolutions and framework/access information otherwise remain unchanged. Table 8 still specifies 400 × 225 for RGB, leaving the resolution documentation inconsistent.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the comparisons with view-transformation and neural-field pre-training approaches. Citation punctuation changes do not add or remove references.

P1.justification: v2 converts citations throughout to parenthetical formatting, adds the conference publication header and slightly shortens Figure 1's caption. Section order and nearly all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds an ICLR 2026 running header and makes small caption, text-flow and table-width adjustments. All figures and tables remain in their corresponding locations, with identical figure imagery and no added panels or table rows.

improvement.justification: Citation formatting improves presentation slightly, but the resolution revision has an uncertain effect on reproducibility. Section 4.2 changes from half-size to quarter-size rendering and Table 7 changes accordingly, while Table 8 retains 400 × 225 RGB evaluation despite the unchanged 800 × 450 inputs. With scores unchanged and no explanation of whether these edits correct reporting or reflect changed evaluations, the PDFs do not support a reliable net-quality judgment.
